doc.title: Kenny Davern interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 16, 2001 [interview 2 of 2]

title: His mother and the Sopranos comparison
summary: Davern compares his ambivalent mother to Tony Soprano's mother on the HBO series and the actress who played her.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: I had a very ambivalent mother. In fact my wife and I bought “The Soprano” series, you know, on HBO, “The Sopranos” series. And it turns out that I really have something in common with Tony Soprano, you know, a/k/a James whatever his name is, he’s very good, that we both had the same mother. Same mother. In fact she even has the same voice.
And the poor woman who played Tony Soprano’s mother died over this past summer I understand.

Marchand, yeah. She was very good. She really knew — it must be a type that a lot of people have for mothers because when he wanted to smother her with a pillow and held it physically, she was on oxygen and they were wheeling her out on a gurney smiling. This
is sort of a curious way of answering your question, Monk, about what music did I hear as a kid. I can’t say other than what was on the airwaves.
